claims.text: The target eutectic HEA contains FCC and ordered B2 phases.
The initial solutionized or as-cast state has minimal LCO development.
Intermediate aging at approximately 400-600°C promotes LCO formation.
LCO formation is kinetically favorable in the intermediate aging regime but does not produce complete ordering.
Impurity segregation is absent in the proposed embrittlement regime.
Aging produces strong Co-Cr-like or analogous LCOs within the B2 phase.
LCOs create high-energy antiphase boundaries and rugged dislocation-energy landscapes.
LCO evolution causes phase-boundary morphological changes that accommodate internal stresses.
LCO-induced energetic roughness impedes and pins dislocations.
High APB energy and complex stacking-fault energy force dislocations to move by nanoscale segment detrapping.
Repeated dislocation pinning and jerky motion occur in concentrated FCC HEAs.
Jerky dislocation motion is specifically diagnostic of LCO-rich ordered domains.
Intermittent dislocation detrapping produces localized stress concentrations and brittle fracture.
At higher aging temperatures, thermal activation enables dislocations to overcome LCO-induced barriers.
At higher temperatures, LCOs may partially disorder and thereby reduce dislocation barriers.
Barrier reduction at higher temperatures restores ductility.
The alloy undergoes a transient loss of ductility at intermediate aging temperatures followed by ductility recovery at higher temperatures.
The embrittlement regime is approximately 400-600°C, with insufficient LCO development below it and thermal barrier reduction or disordering above it.
The transition is not caused by grain-boundary embrittlement or impurity segregation.
A grain-boundary mechanism would produce neither the proposed jerky dislocation behavior nor temperature-induced recovery of ductility.
